ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 6 — Focused Visit (Care-plan review) — Lorraine Hansberry

code.originalText: Six weeks after pancreaticoduodenectomy: pathology, diabetes and enzyme replacement after surgery, and the plan for chemotherapy after surgery

text.paragraph: Review six weeks after pancreaticoduodenectomy: pathology, diabetes, digestion, and the plan for chemotherapy after surgery. [S]

Ms. Hansberry returns six weeks after a pylorus-preserving pancreaticoduodenectomy with resection of a segment of the superior mesenteric vein. She was in hospital nine days; her stomach was slow to empty for the first week and then recovered. Insulin glargine was started four days after surgery when her glucose rose, and her home fasting readings are now 140 to 170 mg/dL on 8 units. She finished four weeks of enoxaparin two weeks ago. Since surgery her stools have been loose and pale after larger meals despite pancrelipase. She has lost 2.4 kg since surgery. Pain is 2 out of 10 at the wound and she rarely needs oxycodone. She is writing again for an hour each morning. Fingertip tingling is barely there. She saw Dr. Adeyemi-Rourke last week, who recommends chemotherapy after surgery starting next week. She has had no thoughts of self-harm. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 2026-10-05; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Thin, well; weight 51.8 kg; blood pressure 106/68, pulse 86
Healed upper midline and right subcostal incision without hernia or redness; soft; mildly tender at the wound
Monofilament sensation and pulses normal; no lesions
Engaged; planning her writing around the treatment days

Epigastric pain for about two months, boring through to the back and worse after meals and lying flat, with nausea, early fullness, a loss of 5 kg (8 percent of her weight), and pale, loose stools: an upper abdominal cause such as a bleeding ulcer or a pancreatic or duodenal tumor must be found. Upper endoscopy and pancreas-protocol CT booked this week
S — Synthetic presenting problem anchored to the documented collapse in pain and the account of a suspected duodenal ulcer. Superseded by the diagnosis at the second visit.
Iron deficiency anemia from chronic upper gastrointestinal blood loss: black stools on and off for three weeks, two near-fainting spells, hemoglobin 9.1 g/dL, MCV 74 fL, ferritin 6 ng/mL
S — Synthetic finding anchored to the documented account that she was told she had anemia and bleeding ulcers.

New hyperglycemia: A1c 6.6% and random glucose 132 mg/dL in a lean woman of 32 who is losing weight; new diabetes with weight loss can be the first sign of a pancreatic cancer, so it is to be confirmed and explained, not labeled type 2
S — Synthetic finding; superseded when diabetes due to the pancreatic cancer was recorded at the second visit.

Adenocarcinoma of the head of the pancreas, 3.1 cm, invading the duodenum, borderline resectable (tumor contact of more than half the circumference of the superior mesenteric vein, no arterial contact), no distant spread, CA 19-9 486 U/mL after biliary drainage; on EUS-guided biopsy; synthetic modern detail linked to her documented cancer, whose primary site the sources record differently
S — Synthetic histology, site, stage and course; the sources say she died of cancer and differ on whether it was pancreatic, duodenal, or colonic with spread to the pancreas (R). See sources.md.
Diabetes due to the pancreatic cancer (pancreatogenic, type 3c): A1c 6.6% at intake and fasting glucose 141 mg/dL
S — Synthetic consequence of the synthetic tumor.
Exocrine pancreatic insufficiency from obstruction of the pancreatic duct: pale, floating, loose stools after fatty meals and weight loss
S — Synthetic consequence of the synthetic tumor; diagnosed clinically, as guidance allows in pancreatic cancer.
Cancer-related pain in the upper abdomen and back, 6 out of 10, with sleep broken by it
S — Synthetic symptom of the synthetic tumor.
Obstruction of the distal common bile duct by the tumor, relieved by a covered metal stent placed at ERCP
S — Synthetic consequence of the synthetic tumor.

Chemotherapy-induced diarrhea from irinotecan, grade 2 (five to six watery stools a day above her usual), starting on day 3 of cycle 5, with low potassium and magnesium and mild dehydration; no fever, blood or neutropenia; resolved
S — Synthetic treatment effect; not a historical claim.

Oxaliplatin peripheral neuropathy, grade 1: tingling in the fingers and toes in the cold, lasting a few days after each cycle, with mild tingling at the fingertips between cycles; no effect on writing or buttons
S — Synthetic common effect of oxaliplatin.
After pylorus-preserving pancreaticoduodenectomy with superior mesenteric vein resection: loss of the head of the pancreas, with more marked exocrine insufficiency and insulin-requiring diabetes
S — Synthetic consequence of the synthetic operation.

list.item:
Pancreatic head adenocarcinoma, ypT2N1, R0 resection after modified FOLFIRINOX (C25.0). A complete resection with clear margins after a partial response. Two lymph nodes were involved, so the risk of return is real. CA 19-9 is now normal at 18 U/mL. Dr. Adeyemi-Rourke recommends chemotherapy after surgery to complete about six months of treatment in all: six more cycles of fluorouracil, leucovorin and irinotecan every two weeks, keeping the reduced irinotecan dose and leaving out oxaliplatin so that the neuropathy does not return in her hands. She agrees. Counts, kidney and liver function allow it. [S]
Cycle 1 after surgery in one week, with pegfilgrastim on day 3.
Apixaban 2.5 mg twice daily again from the first cycle.
After chemotherapy: history, examination, CA 19-9 and CT every three to six months for two years.

After pancreaticoduodenectomy (Z90.411). Loose, pale stools after larger meals mean the enzyme dose is now too low after removal of the head of the pancreas; weight is 6.5 percent below the weight at diagnosis. [S]
Pancrelipase increased to three capsules (108,000 lipase units) with meals and two with snacks.
Dietitian review this week.
Vitamin D level at the next blood test.

Diabetes due to pancreatic disease, now on insulin (E08.9). Glucose 156 mg/dL today and fasting readings 140 to 170 on 8 units of glargine; no lows. Urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio 12 mg/g, normal. [S]
Insulin glargine increased to 10 units at night.
Hypoglycemia teaching repeated, with glucose tablets at her desk.
Dilated eye examination booked for next week.
A1c in December.

Obstruction of the bile duct (K83.1). Relieved: the stent was removed and the bile duct reconnected at surgery; bilirubin 0.5 mg/dL. [S]
Problem resolved.

Oxaliplatin neuropathy, grade 1 (G62.0). Almost resolved; no oxaliplatin is planned. [S]
Review at each visit.

list.item: Endoscopy and pancreas-protocol CT within one week, tissue diagnosis and biliary drainage within two weeks, and a tumor board plan within three weeks of presentation. Outcome by 2026-05-04: Endoscopy in two days, CT in three, EUS biopsy and stent in one week, tumor board in nine days, consultation at two weeks [S]

Germline genetic testing with counseling and tumor molecular profiling resulted before surgery. Outcome by 2026-06-29: Germline panel negative; tumor KRAS G12D, microsatellite stable, no targetable alteration [S]

Six cycles of modified FOLFIRINOX before surgery with no delay of more than one week. Outcome by 2026-08-10: Six cycles; one dose reduction of irinotecan after diarrhea; CT shows a partial response [S]
Resection with clear margins if restaging shows no progression. Outcome by 2026-10-05: Pancreaticoduodenectomy with vein resection; margins clear (R0) [S]
Pain 3 out of 10 or less with a clear head for writing. Outcome by 2026-06-29: Pain 1 to 2 out of 10 on oxycodone 5 mg once or twice a day [S]

Weight kept within 5 percent of the weight at diagnosis through chemotherapy, with enzyme replacement and dietitian support. Outcome by 2026-08-10: Weight 54.2 kg before surgery, 2 percent below the weight at diagnosis [S]
PHQ-9 below 10 throughout treatment, with support she chooses and palliative care alongside cancer treatment. Outcome by 2026-10-05: PHQ-9 between 6 and 8 [S]

Follow-up: Chemotherapy after surgery from next week. Dietitian and eye examination this week and next. Preventive visit in about two weeks. Call for fever of 38.0 °C or more, yellow eyes, low glucose readings, or worsening diarrhea. Next scheduled visit 2026-10-21: periodic adult preventive visit during chemotherapy after surgery. [S]
